title: AlphaDirection1: EEG, ECG, PPG in the resting state and working memory for sequentially and simultaneously presented digits
description: Raw 64-channel EEG, ECG, PPG and behavioral recordings from 30 healthy young adults (18–32 years) during resting state and a verbal working memory digit-span task with serial recall. The resting session alternated eyes-closed and eyes-open blocks followed by passive cartoon viewing. In the working memory task, seven-digit sequences were presented visually either simultaneously or sequentially at different rates and with different inter-stimulus intervals, allowing study of how presentation mode affects neural oscillations and peripheral physiology.
methods_description: EEG (64 channels), ECG and PPG were recorded in BrainVision format. Resting state comprised four 1-minute blocks of eyes-closed and eyes-open rest followed by about 4 minutes of cartoon watching. In the working memory task, participants saw seven-digit sequences in four presentation modes (simultaneous 2800 ms; fast sequential 400 ms per digit; fast with 600 ms ISI; slow sequential 1000 ms per digit) and typed the digits in order on a numpad. Trial-wise accuracy and partial-score measures were computed.
